[WP] The first death in centuries has just occurred..

When cybernetic implants became the norm, people hailed it as an end to the failures of the frail human form. If a part was going bad, just swap it out with one that worked! Augmenting, the process of "upgrading" the human body with cybernetic implants and prosthetics became so commonplace that before long, it wasn't at all unusual to take a stroll along a crowded beach and see as much plastic, metal, and Synth-skin as real flesh and blood. Things only progressed from there, with further advances in augmenting the human brain itself. A delicate organ, the brain was always a tricky subject for Augmenters to approach. You could only do so much, even with bleeding edge technology.

Science, of course, prevailed, by pushing the limits as it always did. By the year 2100, almost every First World Citizen had been augmented in one way or another. Life expectancy rates skyrocketed from an average of 80-100 years to a staggering estimate of three hundred. By 2150, the first "back-up" units had been created. These units, implanted in the human brain itself, scanned and preserved all the information held within the brain: Your personality, your thoughts, your ideas, your memories, your emotions, everything. The human 'soul' was digitized, formatted, and safely stored within the confines of an on-board Black Box. When the body finally failed, when no further augmentation could save the person's life, or in the event of catastrophic failure, the Black Box would immediately uplink with the Network, and safely download all the information it held in the form of a contained Intelligence.

That was the day people stopped dying.

From that point on, any time a person's body gave out, or they had an accident, or were murdered, their very souls were saved in a digital form, to be downloaded into a new body at their convenience. In the intervening centuries, mankind had expanded from beyond the tiny blue marble it called home, and established thriving colonies and populations on Venus, Mars, and several moons throughout the solar system. Since that day, every human being who was ever Augmented with a black box has been alive and well, conscious, aware, and productive members of society in ways our forefathers could never have imagined.

So, I guess you're wondering, where do I fit in here? Why am I telling you all of this? Well, it's necessary, you see, for the sake of my report. My name is Xian Li Hao, Special Detective for the Martian Federation's Hall of Justice. I'm an Augment, just like you, just like every one else in the Sol System.

And today, I've been called on to investigate the first murder...no, the first actual, honest to goodness death, in centuries.

I'm looking at a corpse, a mangled mess of Polycarbonated Graphene, flesh, and fiber optic wiring. No witnesses, no clues, just one very horrifying reality: The Black Box is perfectly in tact, but the victim is nowhere to be found. When the body was found, we ran the serial number on the Box and came up with an ID quickly enough. That alone should have told us exactly where the Victim had been uploaded to, and it did. The only problem was, the victim wasn't there. He wasn't anywhere on the Networks, and when the Techs took a closer look at the box, they were appalled to find that not only had no upload occurred, but that the box itself had been wiped clean: There was no trace of the Soul that had resided within its hardware.

Now I'm faced with the reality of tracking down and apprehending someone who has proven they can kill someone, actually end their existence. I don't know if I'm up to the task. I don't know if anyone is. What I do know is that no matter what, whoever did this has to be stopped. The fact that no one has died for centuries had been a major contributor to peace among the various factions of humanity. Anything that shatters that reality could open the door to assassination, war, and worse, genocide.

I can't let that happen. "Todd," I say, turning to the coroner, who is still studying the body, "What can you tell me?"

"Well," He replied, wiping off his hands, "Not a damned thing."

"Great..."
